<action type="say">
I’m not seeing any emergency plumbing providers available through this system in your area for today, only electrical/HVAC, so I can’t directly book a plumber for you here.

Because there’s active water under the cabinet, take these steps right away:

1) Shut off water to the sink  
- Look under the sink for two small shutoff valves (hot and cold). Turn both clockwise until they stop.  
- If there are no valves or they don’t close, shut off the condo’s main water (often in a utility closet or near the water heater).

2) Contain the leak  
- Clear everything out of the cabinet.  
- Wipe up standing water and place a bucket/bowl under the trap (the U-shaped pipe) or wherever it’s dripping.  
- Put towels at the base of the cabinet and wring/replace as they soak.

3) Be cautious with electricity  
- If there are outlets or appliances in that cabinet, don’t use them until everything is completely dry.

Next, you’ll want to reach a local licensed/insured emergency plumber in Fort Worth (or your building’s maintenance/HOA if it’s covered). When you call, you can say:

“I have an active leak under my kitchen sink at 1234 Main Street, Fort Worth 76102. Water shows up under the cabinet when the sink is running. The condo is about 10–15 years old. I’ve shut off the water to the sink. I need a licensed and insured plumber as soon as possible.”

If you’d like, you can paste in 2–3 plumber names or links you find (Google/Maps/Angi/Thumbtack/etc.), and I’ll help you quickly pick the best one based on reviews, credentials, and pricing notes, or draft a text/email you can send them with all the key details and photos.</action>
